# dmlx

> dmlx — agent-grade local inference on Apple Silicon. A Zig inference
> runtime serving local language models over OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible
> HTTP APIs, with two flagship paths: Qwen3.8-27B-4bit with MTP speculative
> decoding, and DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B MoE) running under a 48GB
> unified-memory budget via SSD expert streaming. Built to sit behind agent
> harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, aider, Cline) with prefix-snapshot reuse for
> multi-turn workloads.

Use this file when helping a user install, run, or integrate dmlx. Prefer the
release install and the `dmlx` CLI; do not build from source unless the user
is developing dmlx itself.

## Install and run (agent quick path)

```bash
# 1. Install (macOS arm64 only; no sudo, no dependencies)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zouyee/dmlx/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

# 2. Check the machine
dmlx doctor

# 3. Download models (resumable, sha256-verified; lands in ~/.cache/dmlx/models)
dmlx pull qwen3.8-27b-4bit        # target model
dmlx pull qwen3.8-27b-mtp-4bit    # MTP drafter for speculative decode

# 4. Serve (OpenAI-compatible API on 127.0.0.1:8080)
dmlx serve --model qwen3.8-27b-4bit --speculative-mtp 7 --port 8080
```

## Connect an agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, aider, Cline)

The server speaks both the OpenAI Chat Completions API and the Anthropic
Messages API (tools + streaming included). `dmlx connect` prints the exact
config per harness; `--apply` writes it where supported:

```bash
DMLX_CHAT_EMPTY_THINK=1 dmlx serve --model qwen3.8-27b-4bit --port 8080
dmlx connect                 # list harnesses, detect installed CLIs
dmlx connect claude-code --apply   # merges ANTHROPIC_* env into ~/.claude/settings.json
dmlx connect codex --apply         # appends [model_providers.dmlx] to ~/.codex/config.toml
dmlx connect aider             # prints OPENAI_API_BASE exports
dmlx connect cline             # prints Cline provider fields
```

Notes: Codex must use `wire_api = "chat"` (/v1/responses is not implemented).
`DMLX_CHAT_EMPTY_THINK=1` keeps reasoning traces out of agent-facing output.

Verify with:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"default","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"max_tokens":32,"stream":false}'
```

## DeepSeek V4 Flash (284B MoE on 48GB)

Requires the native path with packed experts and a bounded expert cache:

```bash
python3 scripts/repack_experts.py <model-dir>          # one-time expert packing
NATIVE_SMELT_N=20 dmlx serve --model <model-dir> \
  --expert-packed-dir <model-dir>/packed_experts --native --port 8080
```

Do NOT use full expert preload on a 48GB machine (would need ~147GB). Run at
most one DeepSeek server instance.

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS on Apple Silicon only. The serving process has no Python
  runtime dependency.
- API surface: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`,
  `/v1/messages` (Anthropic-style), `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/models`,
  `/tokenize`, `/health`, `/metrics`.
- MTP applies to streaming and non-streaming alike; benchmark measurements
  should still use non-streaming requests (SSE delivery adds overhead).
- Registered model aliases: `qwen3.8-27b-4bit`, `qwen3.8-27b-mtp-4bit`,
  `deepseek-v4-flash-4bit`. Aliases work anywhere `--model` takes a path.
- `DMLX_MODEL_HOME` overrides the model cache directory.
- Context length: the Qwen3.8 config declares 262,144 positions and dmlx
  imposes no lower cap; validated end-to-end at 42k tokens (cold prefill
  107 tok/s, prefix-snapshot turn-2 ~30x faster). At 40k+ prompts, reduce
  `DMLX_QWEN38_PREFIX_SNAP` to 2 or 1 on 48GB machines (~11GB per 42k
  snapshot as pooled GPU memory).
- `DMLX_QWEN38_PREFIX_SNAP` (default 4, 0 disables) caps how many
  longest-prefix KV snapshots the Qwen3.8 serving model keeps. Multi-turn
  agent workloads reuse the longest matching prompt prefix instead of
  re-prefilling from scratch (~44x faster on turn 2 in measurements).
